A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Omni2Sound work. All 17 pages of each version, including main Sections 1–7, appendices A–H, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original caption-quality evaluations, audio-generation benchmark results, training ablations, off-screen experiments and human evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including main Tables 1–7, the appendix AudioCaps comparison and the human-study results in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The SoundAtlas construction pipeline, DiT conditioning architecture and three-stage training procedure are retained, including text dropout and off-screen synthesis. Rewriting Sections 3–4 does not establish a change to the algorithm, objectives or model components.

E1.justification: v3 adds AudioAtlas to the evaluation list in Section 6.1, but still calls it a list of three benchmarks and supplies no corresponding protocol or results, including in Appendix E. Actual additional evaluation coverage cannot be established. The demonstrated training and evaluation coverage otherwise remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the caption-quality tables, generation benchmarks, ablations and appendix human study. Newly discussed methods such as OmniSonic are not added to the reported comparisons; corrected bibliographic entries do not establish baseline replacements.

E3.justification: The documented sampling ratios, 1.2M-step ablation budget, audio preprocessing, eight-second evaluation, metrics and human-study procedures remain unchanged. Section 5 replaces 14,000 and 1,048 with less precise descriptions of 14,000+ and 1,000+; this does not establish revised evaluation samples or splits.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same task-mixture and caption-quality ablations, progressive-training comparisons, off-screen synthesis evaluation and unseen-caption generalization test. The appendix cost analysis and qualitative caption examples are also retained without new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Mean win-rate and MOS reporting practices remain unchanged, as do the five-annotator caption evaluation and 16-participant generation study. v3 adds no repeated-run information, seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results in main Tables 1–7, appendix Tables 6–7 and Figure 4 are unchanged. This includes the off-screen win rates of 46.8% and 53.2% and Omni2Sound’s AudioCaps LA-CLAP score of 0.36. No AudioAtlas results are supplied.

T1.justification: The diffusion loss, categorical task-sampling formulation, routing thresholds and Appendix C win-rate formula retain their mathematical content. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three contributions: SoundAtlas, three-stage unified Omni2Sound training and VGGSound-Omni. Claims about human-expert-level captions, fivefold cost reduction, resolving task competition and unified state-of-the-art performance remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the interpretation of aligned VT2A data as a bridge between tasks, the opposing text/video biases and the rationale for decoupled robustness training. The explanation involving HunyuanVideo-Foley’s larger training corpus also remains. No substantive new limitations or applicability qualifications are introduced.

D1.justification: The project-page address changes, and the standalone AV-benchmark repository reference is replaced by a citation to MMAudio, removing its explicit repository link. Appendix implementation settings, preprocessing instructions and captioning prompt remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish any change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including ControlAudio, FreeAudio and OmniSonic, and extends the related-work discussion to joint audio and speech generation. Additional citations cover generative modeling and agent tools. The central positioning around unresolved task competition remains intact; many other reference changes are bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: Sections 2–5 receive extensive paragraph-level rewriting, particularly the SoundAtlas pipeline and all three training stages. v3 removes duplicated wording, regularizes terminology, corrects internal references and extensively revises bibliography text. It also adds acknowledgments and changes author order, while retaining the overall section structure.

P2.justification: The figures and table structures are retained. Limited presentation changes include tightening the main Table 7 caption and correcting its benchmark spelling, local text and table reflow, and altered bibliography layout. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability and traceability by tightening the method exposition, removing a duplicated training-schedule sentence, and correcting references to SoundAtlas’s section, the Video-LLaMA results table and AudioX. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. The unsupported AudioAtlas evaluation mention introduces an inconsistency, limiting the gains to a modest overall presentation improvement.
